milestone.title: raul Path tab rework — 2-line description preview + stage chip + status overlay

intent.outcome: Every milestone in the raul Path tab renders as 2 visual lines: a title line carrying the id, title, current mp-flow stage chip (`[N/12]` from M202's flow_stages), priority glyph, age, and (when set) a status overlay chip for blocked / cancelled / deferred; plus a preview line carrying the first line of `intent.outcome` truncated to ~80 chars with a `↳` prefix. The tree structure (trunk + branches + blocked fork) is preserved. Operators scanning the Path tree see what each milestone is about without opening detail.

problem.description: Today's Path tab renderer (`crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs`) renders each milestone as a single line carrying only id + title + a short `detail` token (e.g. step id). After M202 introduced the per-milestone `flow_stages` map and M203 introduced the 2nd-line description preview pattern for Backlog/Ideas, the Path tab is the odd one out: it shows none of the new signals. Operators get the tree shape (which is genuinely useful) but no hint of what each milestone is about, what stage it's in, or whether it's blocked / cancelled / deferred beyond the implicit 'this is on the blocked branch' signal. The Path tab feels under-enriched relative to the Milestones / Backlog / Ideas tabs that landed M202 and M203.

in_scope: Update `trunk_item_line` and `flat_branch_lines` in `crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs` to emit 2 visual lines per milestone. Title line carries: id, title, stage chip `[N/12]` (from `flow_stages`, same computation as M202's Stage cell), priority glyph (urgent / high / normal / low), age (relative time via `humanize::humanize_relative` against created or updated), and the existing `◀ next` indicator on the first execution item. Preview line carries the first line of `intent.outcome` truncated to ~80 chars with a `↳` prefix in dim color.
Update `blocked_lines` to render 2 lines per blocked milestone too. The existing `blocker: M<n>` annotation on the title line stays; the preview line carries `intent.outcome` first line.

Status overlay chip on the title line: when the milestone has `blocked: true`, render a `⚠ blocked` chip; for `cancelled: true`, `⊘ cancelled`; for `deferred: true`, `⏸ deferred`. Multiple overlays: priority is blocked > cancelled > deferred (blocked wins; same precedence as the existing badge rendering). Color: blocked uses palette danger, cancelled uses palette warn, deferred uses palette dim.

Stage chip text: derive from `flow_stages` (current mp-flow stage). Same logic as `progress::stage_cell_line` / M202 Stage column. Falls back to `lifecycle` text when `flow_stages` is empty (legacy milestone that hasn't had a transition yet).
Empty preview behavior: when `intent.outcome` is empty or only whitespace, the preview line renders only the `↳` prefix (no `(no description)` placeholder). Matches M203's resolved collapse behavior.

Tree structure preservation: the `├─` / `└─` / `│` / `●` connector logic stays. Spines between trunk items stay. Branch headers (BLOCKED / AWAITING-APPROVAL / GROOMING / REVIEW) keep their bold color and item-count suffix.
Compact-mode handling: same 2-line layout at narrower terminal widths. Truncation kicks in earlier on the preview line due to less horizontal space. The spine characters and tree connectors stay.

Tests: unit (`intent.outcome` first-line extraction; truncation at 80 chars; status-overlay precedence; stage chip text derivation from flow_stages); TUI snapshot (2-line per item; preview line dim + ↳ prefix; status overlay chip; tree structure intact at width 120 and width 80).
out_of_scope: Filter modal on the Path tab (separate milestone; reuses M204 framework).
Configurable profiles (compact / default / detailed) on Path — separate milestone.
Sort changes — Path is tree-ordered, not list-sorted; sort keys from M205 don't apply.
Changes to the data model — no new fields. Uses existing `flow_stages` (M202), `intent.outcome` (existing), `priority`, `created`/`updated`, blocked/cancelled/deferred overlays.
Changes to the branch fork logic — blocked items still fork at their blocker; the structure stays.
Drag-and-drop, expand/collapse of tree nodes — tree is always fully expanded; scroll handles overflow.
Changes to `path_tree_model` shape — the renderer is the only thing that changes; the model stays.
Adding `intent.outcome` to the data model — it already exists on every milestone; this slice only renders it.

design_decisions.rationale: Matches the M203 Backlog/Ideas rework pattern. Half as many items visible but 2× the info per item. The Path tab is for scanning the bigger picture, not deep inspection, so the loss in item count is acceptable.
intent.outcome already exists on every milestone. It's the 'what is this milestone about' prose. First-line truncation gives a meaningful preview without needing a new field.

design_decisions.choice: flow_stages (current mp-flow stage) with lifecycle fallback
design_decisions.rationale: Same computation as M202's Stage column. flow_stages carries the per-stage map; lifecycle is the fallback for legacy milestones that haven't had a transition yet. Single source of truth via the Stage column helper.
Matches the existing badge rendering precedence in the codebase. Blocked is the most urgent state — should be the visible overlay when multiple are set.

design_decisions.choice: Preview line renders only the ↳ prefix when intent.outcome is empty
design_decisions.rationale: Matches M203's resolved collapse behavior. No `(no description)` placeholder — keeps the visual rhythm consistent across rows.

The trunk + branches + blocked fork shape is the value proposition of the Path tab. Operators depend on the tree visual to understand the bigger picture. The visual enrichment (more info per item) sits on top of the existing structure.
Filter modal reuses the M204 framework (unified UX across tabs). Folding it into this slice would expand scope and tangle the visual enrichment with the filter UX. Better as its own milestone.
Profile selection is a configurator UX on top of the visual enrichment. The 2-line layout is one profile; adding compact and detailed is additive but not required for this slice.

design_decisions.choice: Keep on title line, after the status overlay chip. The detail (e.g. step: S1.1) is the most actionable field for execution items; it belongs on the title line even at the cost of crowded layout at narrow widths. Compact mode truncates the detail gracefully.
design_decisions.rationale: Operators working the execution trunk need the step id at a glance. Moving it to the preview line buries it under the description.

design_decisions.choice: Use lifecycle_at (RFC3339) as the primary source. Falls back to updated (YYYY-MM-DD) when lifecycle_at is empty (legacy milestone that has never had a transition). Matches M204 age filter semantics for Milestones.
design_decisions.rationale: Consistent with the M204 age filter which uses lifecycle_at for Milestones. RFC3339 gives precise relative time; updated is the less-precise fallback.

open_questions.question: Should the preview line be present for milestones in the BLOCKED branch (where the blocker is the dominant signal) or skipped to keep the visual rhythm tight?
open_questions.answer: Superseded by Q-02 resolution: every milestone renders 2 lines regardless of branch. Q-02 wins.

open_questions.question: For blocked items, the title line already carries `blocker: M<n>` plus the blocked overlay chip. Does the preview line add value there, or should it be suppressed?
open_questions.answer: Always render preview for all milestones regardless of branch. Visual rhythm stays consistent; BLOCKED branch and execution trunk have the same line count per item. The blocker annotation and blocked chip on the title line carry the BLOCKED-specific signal; the preview line carries the description.

findings.description: Per-AC evidence discipline failure (third occurrence). Runner set all 12 ACs evidence to generic 'milestone complete' string instead of per-AC command + exit code + test count. Same defect pattern as M200 F-12 and M201 F-05. Reviewer restored per-AC evidence via mp milestone criterion pass as side-effect: AC-01..AC-11 carry 'cargo nextest run ... exit 0 (N/N pass)'; AC-12 carries 'make test exit 0 (3316 tests pass cold-cache; 1/3316 failed on retry due to pre-existing flaky mp::watch::bridge::tests::run_herdr_with_timeout_kills_entire_process_group unrelated to M206; standalone cargo nextest run -p mp --no-fail-fast exit 0 (2272/2272 pass), cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast exit 0 (950/950 pass)'. Recommend guardrail: mp could refuse 'milestone complete' as evidence and require verification command + exit code + count - backlog item.

Detail field placement contradicts spec. Spec (S1.1 action + design_decisions 'Detail field placement') says 'Detail field stays on the title line after the status overlay chip.' Implementation in trunk_item_rows (crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs:461-466), flat_branch_lines (crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs:541-546), and blocked_lines (crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs:628-633) places the detail BEFORE the overlay chip. Order in trunk_item_rows is: label → stage chip → priority → age → detail → overlay chip → ◀ next; spec says detail should come after overlay chip. No AC or test exercises this ordering, so the drift is spec-implementation mismatch without behavior coverage gap. The visual difference is small but the spec text is explicit.

Two dead pub functions with WRONG color mappings contradict AC-03. crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs:311-335 overlay_chip: spec (AC-03) wants blocked=danger, cancelled=warn, deferred=dim; code returns blocked=danger, cancelled=danger, deferred=warn. Function is pub, never called from production or tests, and contains dead code 'let m = item["milestone"].clone(); let _ = m;' (no-op clone). crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs:339-350 overlay_chip_color: same wrong mapping (danger/danger/warn) and a misleading 'We carry two channels' comment that describes an API surface that does not exist. The correct version is overlay_chip_pair (path_view.rs:355-371) which is what the row emitters actually call. Either delete the dead functions or fix their color mappings and comments. Currently they sit next to the correct code and will burn any future caller who picks the shorter-named version.
